questions.q: What happens, mechanically, with a Live connection every time you interact with a view?
options: Tableau sends a new query straight to the underlying data source
Tableau reads from a local .hyper file copy
Tableau refreshes a cached extract automatically
Nothing — Live connections only update once per day
questions.explain: A Live connection means Tableau queries the actual source directly on every interaction — there's no local copy of the data.

options: A local snapshot of the data stored in Tableau's Hyper engine, queried instead of the original source
A live, always-current window directly into the source database
A type of calculated field
A special kind of join between two tables
questions.explain: An Extract pulls a snapshot out of the source and stores it locally in Tableau's optimized Hyper format, which the view then queries instead of the original source.

questions.q: What is a genuine downside of using an Extract instead of a Live connection?
options: Data goes stale the moment the source changes, until you refresh the extract
Extracts cannot be used offline
Extracts are always slower than Live connections
Extracts cannot be created from SQL Server data
questions.explain: The tradeoff for an Extract's speed and portability is that its data is a snapshot — it won't reflect source changes until refreshed.

questions.q: In the Tableau architecture diagram, which two paths represent the Live vs. Extract choice?
options: The direct SQL Connector path (live) versus the Tableau Data Engine path (extract)
The Gateway versus the Customer/Client layer
The Web versus Mobile client paths
There is only one path — the diagram doesn't distinguish them
questions.explain: The diagram shows Data Connectors splitting into a direct SQL Connector (live queries) and the Tableau Data Engine (extract storage), both eventually reaching VizQL Server.

questions.q: In which situation is using an Extract effectively required, not just preferred?
options: Publishing a workbook to Tableau Public, which does not allow live database connections
Any time you connect to an Excel file
Any time more than one person will view the dashboard
Whenever a workbook contains a calculated field
questions.explain: Tableau Public does not support live connections to databases, so an Extract is required for any workbook published there.
